backlog.spec: Replace the greedy radius code with a single SLSQP solve over the 78 variables (26 centers and 26 radii). Maximize sum(r) subject to pairwise constraints (xi-xj)^2+(yi-yj)^2 >= (ri+rj)^2 for all pairs, and boundary constraints ri <= xi <= 1-ri and ri <= yi <= 1-ri. Start from a seeded random or lattice-jittered configuration with small radii. Supply analytic Jacobians for the constraints and the objective. Shrink the final radii by 1e-9 before returning.
backlog.title: Joint SLSQP over centers and radii

backlog.spec: Keep the centers fixed and solve for the radii as a linear program with scipy.optimize.linprog: maximize sum(r) subject to r_i + r_j <= d_ij for every pair and r_i <= min(x_i, y_i, 1-x_i, 1-y_i). This gives the exact optimal radii for a given layout, replacing the current scaling loop. Use it as the evaluation function inside any center search.
backlog.title: LP radius refinement for fixed centers

backlog.spec: Optimize the 78 variables with L-BFGS-B on the objective -sum(r) + mu * (sum of squared pairwise overlap violations + squared boundary violations). Run a continuation schedule: start mu=10, multiply by 10 each stage up to about 1e7, warm-starting each stage from the previous solution. Finish with a feasibility repair that scales radii down until no overlap remains.
backlog.title: Penalty L-BFGS with geometric mu continuation

backlog.spec: Use a Lubachevsky-Stillinger style relaxation: start with random centers and small radii, then repeatedly take gradient steps that reduce overlap energy while slowly increasing all radii toward a target. Grow radii by a factor each epoch, and when overlap energy exceeds a threshold, shrink the growth rate. Stop when growth stalls and return the feasible radii after a final exact pairwise scaling.
backlog.title: Soft-sphere growth with increasing radius schedule

backlog.spec: Start from a locally optimized packing, then repeat for a fixed number of iterations: perturb 1 to 3 randomly chosen centers by a Gaussian step of scale 0.1 (seeded), re-solve the joint radius-and-center optimization with SLSQP, and accept the new configuration if the sum of radii improves (Metropolis acceptance with a small temperature otherwise). Keep the best configuration seen.
backlog.title: Basin hopping with local SLSQP polish

backlog.spec: After an optimization round, find the circle with the smallest radius, remove it, and find the largest empty spot in the square by evaluating the distance-to-nearest-circle field on a 200x200 grid. Insert the circle at that spot and re-optimize all variables with SLSQP. Accept the move only if the total sum improves; repeat for a fixed number of moves.
backlog.title: Remove-and-reinsert the smallest circle

backlog.spec: Run the full optimization pipeline from many independent random initializations drawn from a fixed-seed numpy Generator, with centers uniform in [0.05, 0.95]^2. Keep the packing with the largest valid sum of radii. Budget the number of starts so the whole run finishes in under four minutes, using a fixed count rather than the wall clock so results are repeatable.
backlog.title: Multi-start with seeded random inits and keep best

backlog.spec: Initialize centers on a staggered row pattern (for example rows of 5, 6, 5, 5, 5 circles, alternating offsets by half a spacing), then add seeded Gaussian jitter of scale 0.02 to every center. Feed this start into the joint optimizer. The aim is to start near dense hexagonal-like structures while letting edge effects reshape the boundary circles.
backlog.title: Hex-like jittered row initialization

backlog.spec: Seed the initial layout with large circles near the center and smaller circles placed at the four corners and along the four edges, following a known good pattern of mixed sizes. Assign initial radii according to this pattern, then run the joint optimizer so the sizes can adjust freely. This targets the boundary effects that a uniform start misses.
backlog.title: Corner and edge seeded layout with mixed sizes

backlog.spec: Initialize radii from a two-cluster distribution (for example 6 large radii near 0.12 and 20 small radii near 0.07) with seeded random centers. Run the joint SLSQP optimizer from this start. Repeat with several different cluster counts and keep the best final packing, which explores different size distributions than a uniform start.
backlog.title: Bimodal radius initialization

backlog.spec: Constrain the layout to be symmetric about the vertical line x = 0.5, so that 13 circles are free and their mirror images are determined, with a possible central circle on the axis. Optimize the reduced variable set with SLSQP, then expand to the full 26 circles and run one unconstrained polish. The reduced problem is smaller and faster to search widely.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric search with half the variables

backlog.spec: Impose fourfold rotational symmetry about the square center: one circle at the center, and the remaining 25 circles arranged in orbits of four under 90-degree rotation (so 25 is not divisible by 4, so allow a fixed extra circle or use a two-fold symmetry instead). Parameterize the free orbit representatives, optimize with SLSQP, and expand. Then run an unconstrained polish on all 26 centers and radii.
backlog.title: Diagonal and 90-degree rotational symmetry

backlog.spec: Split the 26 circles into a small number of groups (for example 2 or 3 groups by initial position). Optimize each group inside a sub-rectangle of the unit square with SLSQP, then place the sub-rectangles together and run a joint optimization over all 26 circles from this merged start. This decomposition gives a structured starting point for the global solve.
backlog.title: Hierarchical cluster-then-merge

backlog.spec: Rewrite the overlap and constraint computations with numpy broadcasting over the full pairwise difference tensor of shape (26, 26, 2), computing all distances and violations at once with no Python loops. Use the precomputed index pairs for the upper triangle. This speeds every objective and constraint evaluation, so the optimizer can run more starts or iterations within the time limit.
backlog.title: Vectorized pairwise constraint evaluation

backlog.spec: Hold a batch of, for example, 16 candidate configurations as one array of shape (16, 26, 2) and apply a single vectorized gradient-ascent step to all of them at once on the penalty objective with a shared step size. Keep the best feasible configuration after each batch step. This amortizes Python overhead and increases the number of explored layouts per second.
backlog.title: Batch of configurations optimized in lockstep

backlog.spec: For the penalty objective, evaluate the overlap penalty each step on a random subset of about one third of the 325 pairs (seeded), rather than all pairs, while the boundary penalty uses all circles. Rescale the stochastic gradient accordingly. This reduces per-step cost, and a final full-pair feasibility pass guarantees validity.
backlog.title: Mini-batch of random pair constraints

backlog.spec: Maximize a smooth surrogate of the radius sum where each overlap constraint uses a softplus or log-sum-exp penalty with temperature beta. Optimize centers with Adam (learning rate about 0.01, seeded initialization) while beta is increased geometrically from about 10 to 1000. Radii are computed from the current centers by an exact LP or greedy step, and the best feasible packing is tracked.
backlog.title: Adam on softened radius sum with temperature annealing

backlog.spec: Run an iterative repulsion relaxation where each circle's update step is scaled by its current radius, so larger circles move more slowly and smaller circles move more freely. Radii are updated each iteration to the largest feasible value given current centers and then scaled up by a small factor. Iterate with a decaying global step and stop when the sum of radii stabilizes.
backlog.title: Per-circle step size proportional to radius

backlog.spec: After a coarse SLSQP solution, polish the joint centers-and-radii problem with scipy.optimize.minimize using method trust-constr, with the same pairwise and boundary constraints expressed as NonlinearConstraint objects that include analytic Jacobians. Accept the polished result only if it is feasible within 1e-12 after shrinking radii by 1e-9. This refines the last digits of the sum.
backlog.title: Trust-constr final polish

backlog.spec: Phase one fixes a common radius r for all circles and maximizes r via a feasibility bisection or SLSQP on the centers only. Phase two releases the individual radii and re-optimizes the centers and radii jointly from the phase-one layout. The equal-radius solution gives a well-spread start, and the second phase lets radii differentiate to increase the total.
backlog.title: Two-phase equal-radius then free-radius solve

backlog.spec: Run a simulated-annealing-style search over centers: at each step perturb all centers with Gaussian noise whose standard deviation decays geometrically from 0.05 to 0.0005 over the run. Evaluate each candidate by the exact LP radii for those centers, and accept by the Metropolis rule with a temperature that also decays. Keep the best configuration. Use a fixed seed.
backlog.title: Annealed perturbation amplitude

backlog.spec: During an early phase, add a weak quadratic penalty pulling each center toward the square center (0.5, 0.5) so the packing compacts into the middle, then reduce that coefficient to zero over several stages and finish with the unconstrained joint solve. This discourages early circles from getting stuck at the boundary in poor positions.
backlog.title: Inward pull then release regularization

backlog.spec: In early optimization stages, freeze a random subset of about 30 percent of the circles (seeded choice each stage) at their current positions and optimize only the rest, then unfreeze all and optimize jointly. This is analogous to dropout and helps the free circles find room around a stable skeleton of already placed circles.
backlog.title: Random freezing of circles during early stages

backlog.spec: Before returning, verify the packing with exact double-precision checks: every circle inside [0,1]^2 and every pairwise distance at least ri + rj. Compute the minimum slack across all constraints and shrink all radii by a margin slightly larger than the worst violation plus 1e-12, so the reported sum equals the sum of the returned radii and the packing is strictly valid.
backlog.title: Safety margin and exact verification

backlog.spec: Maximize a weighted sum sum(w_i r_i) with random positive weights w_i drawn from a seeded distribution (for example uniform in [0.8, 1.2]) for several restarts, then re-solve with all weights equal to 1 starting from the best weighted solution. Varying the weights steers the search toward different size profiles, and the final unweighted polish keeps the true objective.
backlog.title: Random objective weights to diversify radii

backlog.spec: Starting from any feasible packing, repeatedly sweep through circles in a fixed order and grow each radius to the maximum value allowed by its current neighbors and the walls, moving to the next circle when no growth is possible. Alternate with small random center shifts of the most constrained circles. Stop when a full sweep yields no gain. This is a cheap local improvement step applied at the end of every candidate.
backlog.title: Greedy radius growth sweep

backlog.spec: Run the optimization pipeline in a loop of restarts with a fixed count chosen so the full run is about three minutes on one CPU thread, measured by the number of evaluations rather than the clock. Stop early if the best sum has not improved for a set number of consecutive restarts. This keeps the result deterministic under a fixed seed while using the available budget well.
backlog.title: Time-independent restart budget with early stopping

backlog.spec: Run the existing joint SLSQP on 27 circles (same bounds and constraint builders, with n as a parameter) from several seeded starts. For each 27-circle solution, try removing each circle in turn, keep the 26 remaining centers and radii as the start, and re-run SLSQP on 26 circles. Keep the best feasible result after _repair. Budget the loop with the existing time checks so the total stays under about 4 minutes, and fall back to the current multi-start if no 27-circle run finishes.
backlog.title: Drop-one from a 27-circle optimum

backlog.spec: Solve a 25-circle packing with the joint SLSQP from seeded starts. Then find the largest empty hole: evaluate a grid of candidate points (for example 60x60 over the unit square), and for each compute the distance to the nearest circle edge, which gives the largest radius a new circle could have there. Insert the 26th circle at the best candidate with that radius, and re-run joint SLSQP on all 26 circles. Keep the best feasible result after _repair, and repeat with the top few holes.
backlog.title: Add-one into the largest hole from a 25-circle optimum

backlog.spec: Maintain a small population (about 6 to 8) of feasible 26-circle packings from the existing multi-start. Create children by cutting two parents with a random vertical or horizontal line: take the circles of parent A on one side and the circles of parent B on the other, then fix the count to 26 by dropping the closest-overlapping circles or adding random ones. Re-optimize each child with joint SLSQP after a short _relax, insert it into the population if it beats the worst member, and iterate until the time budget is spent. Use a fixed seed.
backlog.title: Genetic crossover of packings

backlog.spec: Generate many random starts (about 200), each with a cheap evaluation: a short _relax pass followed by one SLSQP run capped at a low maxiter (about 40). Rank all starts by the resulting sum of radii, keep the top 10 percent, and give those survivors a full SLSQP with maxiter 300 and ftol 1e-12. Repeat the halving once more on the survivors if time allows. Return the best feasible result after _repair. The fixed seed keeps the run repeatable.
backlog.title: Successive halving over many cheap starts

backlog.spec: After the final SLSQP, identify the active set: pair constraints with gap below 1e-7 and containment constraints with slack below 1e-7. Count the active constraints and unknowns (2n centers plus n radii, 78 total). If the active set is square or overdetermined, solve the KKT-style system with a Gauss-Newton or Levenberg-Marquardt step on the active constraints, holding the objective stationary using the Lagrange multipliers from the SLSQP result. Accept the Newton result only if it stays feasible within 1e-12 and increases the sum; otherwise keep the SLSQP output. Then apply _repair.
backlog.title: Active-set Newton polish

backlog.spec: Replace the hard pair and boundary constraints in an unconstrained-by-SLSQP stage with a smooth penalty: for each constraint g_k >= 0, use softplus-based penalty -(1/beta) log(sum exp(-beta g_k)) or a plain squared hinge. Maximize the sum of radii minus a penalty weight times total violation using L-BFGS-B with analytic gradients. Increase the sharpness beta geometrically (for example from 5 to 1e4) across about 6 stages, warm-starting each stage. Finish with the existing joint SLSQP and _repair. This is a different smoothing than the penalty mu continuation already tried.
backlog.title: Log-sum-exp smoothed constraints with annealed sharpness

backlog.spec: Build the starting layout by a weighted Lloyd iteration. Draw random seeded points, assign each a weight that grows toward the square center (for example w = 1 + 0.6 * (1 - distance to center / max distance)), and iterate about 30 times: compute the power (weighted) Voronoi cells over a fine sample grid, then move each center to its cell centroid. Set each initial radius to the distance from the center to its nearest-cell boundary, scaled by 0.8. Pass these centers and radii into the existing _optimize and _repair. This produces a mixed-size start with large circles near the middle and small ones near the edges.
backlog.title: Power-diagram density-matched initialization

backlog.spec: Take the best mirror-symmetric packing from _sym_search (already computed in the multi-start) and use it as the start for a free optimization. Add a random perturbation of amplitude 1e-3 to all centers and radii, with a different seed for each of about 5 perturbations, then run the joint _optimize without symmetry constraints. Keep the best feasible result after _repair. Only run this chain if the symmetric solution has a sum above 2.6, so it targets the incumbent basin rather than replacing the whole search.
backlog.title: Symmetry-breaking chain from the mirror optimum

backlog.spec: Instead of hand-placed rings, generate starts from concentric shells parameterized by counts. Choose a random composition of 26 circles into an outer boundary shell (about 14 to 18 circles spaced evenly along the square perimeter, inset by their radius) and one or two inner shells of the remainder placed on scaled, rotated grids. Assign radii from a random bimodal rule (larger inside, smaller on the boundary). Pass each start through the existing _relax and _optimize, keep the best after _repair, and sample the shell counts from the seeded RNG so each start uses a different composition.
backlog.title: Ring-shell initialization with varied shell counts

backlog.spec: Speed up the SLSQP evaluations so more starts fit in the budget. At the start of each _optimize call, build a neighbor list of pairs whose center distance is less than 2 * 0.35 plus a margin of 0.1, and restrict the pair constraints and their Jacobian rows to that list. After each SLSQP run, recompute the neighbor list from the new centers and re-run once if any pair outside the list now overlaps (check with the full pair set, then _repair). This is a proximity-based active set, unlike the random pair subsets tried before, and it reduces the constraint matrix to a few dozen rows.
backlog.title: Neighbor-list pruning of pair constraints

backlog.spec: After the multi-start, take the best packing (x, y, r) and maximize sum(r) + mu * sum(log(slack)) over all pair slacks (d_ij^2 - (r_i + r_j)^2) and wall slacks (x-r, 1-x-r, y-r, 1-y-r), using scipy.optimize.minimize with method L-BFGS-B and analytic gradients. Start at mu = 1e-2 and shrink mu by a factor of 0.1 per stage down to about 1e-8, warm-starting each stage from the previous solution. Keep only strictly interior iterates, so every intermediate point is feasible. Finish with a short joint SLSQP solve and the existing _repair, and keep the result only if its sum beats the incumbent.
backlog.title: Log-barrier interior-point polish

backlog.spec: Add a second symmetric search alongside the mirror search: 26 circles with 13 free circles and their images under the point reflection (x, y, r) -> (1-x, 1-y, r), so no circle sits at the center. Build the affine map from 13 free (x, y, r) triples to the 26 full triples, the same way _sym_layout builds the mirror map, and run SLSQP over the reduced variables with the pair and wall constraints expanded through that map. Seed with random positions in the lower-left half. Run about 6 seeds, then polish the best with the unconstrained _optimize and _repair, and keep it only if it beats the incumbent.
backlog.title: Point-symmetric (180-degree) search

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed unit-square boundary with a container [0, L] x [0, L] that starts large (L = 1.25) and is shrunk toward L = 1 over about 8 stages. At each stage, run joint SLSQP with wall bounds set to the current L, then rescale the centers to the new container. After L reaches 1, do one final joint SLSQP with the true unit bounds and _repair. This lets the circles settle into a looser arrangement and then be squeezed, which is a different path from the inward pull and the penalty continuation already tried.
backlog.title: Shrinking-container schedule

backlog.spec: Polish the best packing by maximizing sum(r) subject to the pair and wall constraints using an augmented Lagrangian. Keep a multiplier vector lambda for each constraint g_k(z) >= 0 and minimize -sum(r) + sum_k (rho/2) * max(0, lambda_k/rho - g_k(z))^2 - lambda_k^2 / (2 rho) with L-BFGS-B and analytic gradients (the same constraint Jacobian as _optimize). After each inner solve, set lambda_k = max(0, lambda_k - rho * g_k), and increase rho by 3x if the max violation has not shrunk by 4x. Run about 10 outer iterations, then apply _repair and keep the result only if it beats the incumbent.
backlog.title: Augmented-Lagrangian polish

backlog.spec: Add a start family based on a square lattice rather than rings or hex rows. Place 5 rows of 5 circles on a jittered 5x5 grid, then add the 26th circle at a random location and let the relaxation and joint SLSQP resolve the defects. Alternatively, use a 6x5 grid of 30 points and delete 4 at random, with a seeded RNG. Each start gets a random jitter scale in [0.01, 0.04] and an initial radius of about 0.08. Feed these starts into the existing multi-start loop in place of 3 of the 12 random starts, and keep the best feasible result.
backlog.title: Square-grid defect start

backlog.spec: From the best packing, repeatedly pick a random subset of about 40 percent of the circles (seeded RNG) and freeze the rest at their current centers and radii. Run joint SLSQP only on the free circles, with the frozen circles included as fixed constraints, so the problem is smaller and fast. Use the joint _optimize with bounds pinned for frozen indices, then _repair on the full set. Accept the new packing if its total sum is at least the incumbent's, or with a small Metropolis probability otherwise. Run about 40 such iterations within the time budget and keep the best. This is a neighbourhood search over subsets, not over single-circle perturbations.
backlog.title: Large-neighborhood search with frozen subsets

backlog.spec: Extend the basin-hopping phase with a move that swaps the positions of two circles of different radii. Pick a random pair (i, j) with a large radius gap, exchange their centers while keeping each circle's radius attached to its index, then re-solve with joint SLSQP starting from the swapped configuration and apply _repair. Interleave swap moves with the current small-jitter moves at a 1:2 ratio. Accept by the existing Metropolis rule with temperature 0.01. Keep the best overall packing. This explores assignments of sizes to positions, which the jitter-only moves never test.
backlog.title: Swap-move basin hopping

backlog.spec: Speed up the random multi-start by vectorizing _relax across K = 16 configurations at once. Store centers as an array of shape (K, n, 2) and radii as (K, n), and compute all pairwise distances with numpy broadcasting on the (K, n, n) tensor in one pass per iteration, applying the same radius-scaled repulsion, clipping, and radius update as the scalar code. Use a fixed iteration count of about 150 with no early-exit wall-clock check. Then run joint SLSQP on each of the K results. The goal is to double or triple the number of starts that fit in the time budget, keeping the same selection rule.
backlog.title: Lockstep vectorized relaxation for more starts

backlog.spec: Polish the best packing exactly by identifying the active constraints. A constraint is active if its slack is below 1e-7 after SLSQP. Treat the active pair-contact and wall-contact equations as equalities, g_k(x, y, r) = 0, and solve them with Newton's method (Gauss-Newton with np.linalg.lstsq) starting from the current point. Use the active set's Jacobian, and fix the rattlers, meaning circles with no active constraints, at their current positions. Iterate until the residual falls below 1e-13. Then apply a tiny uniform radius shrink of 1e-12 and verify all pair and wall constraints before returning. Keep the result only if it is feasible and beats the incumbent.
backlog.title: Active-set Newton KKT polish

backlog.spec: After each SLSQP solve, classify the circles as rattlers if they have no constraint with slack below 1e-6, meaning they do not carry load. In basin hopping, perturb only the rattlers: move each rattler to a random point chosen from the largest empty region, found by sampling 2000 seeded random points and keeping the one with the greatest distance to all centers and walls, then re-solve with joint SLSQP. If there are no rattlers, fall back to the current 1-3 circle jitter. This targets the slack in the packing directly and avoids disturbing the load-bearing circles, unlike the generic remove-and-reinsert moves tried before.
backlog.title: Rattler-targeted perturbation

backlog.spec: Replace the random multi-start with a seeded (rng seed fixed) CMA-ES-style evolution strategy written in numpy: maintain a Gaussian over the 52 center coordinates (mean initialized from a random feasible layout, step size 0.1, population about 16, weighted recombination of the top half, rank-one and rank-mu covariance updates). For each candidate, clip centers to [0,1], compute radii by solving the LP max sum r subject to r_i + r_j <= d_ij and r_i <= wall distance using scipy.optimize.linprog (highs), and use the LP value as fitness. Run until about 120 seconds of wall time, then polish the best centers with the existing joint SLSQP and _repair. Keep the existing mirror-symmetric phase as a seed for the initial mean.
backlog.title: CMA-ES outer search over centers with inner LP for radii

backlog.spec: Add a seeded differential-evolution population (size about 40) over the 52 center coordinates, with radii always recomputed by a fast feasibility projection (the existing pairwise shrink loop, vectorized with numpy broadcasting). Use DE/rand/1/bin with F = 0.6 and CR = 0.9, and fitness = sum of projected radii. After 60 generations, take the top 5 members and run the existing _optimize followed by _repair on each, keeping the best. This replaces the random multi-start block and keeps all other phases unchanged.
backlog.title: Differential evolution over centers with SLSQP polish

backlog.spec: Generate a set of hex-lattice points covering the unit square with spacing chosen so that about 28 to 30 points fall inside [0,1]^2, using rows offset by half a spacing. Pick a seeded random subset of exactly 26 points by deleting the surplus points, with the deletion favoring points near the boundary or near the center in alternating trials. Use these 26 points as centers, set initial radii to 0.08, run _relax then _optimize then _repair, and keep the best over 10 such seeded trials. This gives a lattice-derived family of starts distinct from jittered rows and the two-ring placement.
backlog.title: Hexagonal lattice start with random vacancies

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random center initializations in the random multi-start phase with a low-discrepancy sequence: generate 26x2 points per start from a scrambled Halton sequence (bases 2 and 3, with a fixed seeded digit permutation) mapped into [0.05, 0.95]^2. Use 40 such starts instead of 12, but run only _relax with iters=40 as a cheap filter, then run _optimize and _repair on the best 8 by relaxed sum. Keep the seed fixed for repeatability.
backlog.title: Quasi-random Sobol-style multi-start

backlog.spec: Inside _optimize, replace the plain sum-of-radii objective with sum(r) + tau * sum(log(r + 1e-9)), solved as a sequence of SLSQP problems with tau annealed geometrically from 0.05 down to 1e-6 (about 6 stages, warm-starting each stage from the previous solution). The log term keeps radii away from zero during early stages, which lets the centers reorganize before small circles are squeezed out; the final stage is the unmodified objective. Apply this to the random multi-start starts only; leave the basin-hopping polish unchanged.
backlog.title: Objective homotopy with a log-radius barrier

backlog.spec: Replace the single Metropolis chain in the basin-hopping loop with 4 replicas at fixed temperatures 0.002, 0.005, 0.012 and 0.03, each holding its own current packing. In each sweep, every replica proposes a move (perturb 1 to 3 centers by normal noise of scale 0.1, re-solve with _optimize and _repair) and accepts by the Metropolis rule at its own temperature. After each sweep, attempt a swap between adjacent temperature replicas with the standard exchange probability. Track the global best across all replicas. Keep a fixed number of sweeps (about 40) and a fixed seed so the run is repeatable.
backlog.title: Parallel tempering over basin-hopping replicas

backlog.spec: Before the square-container optimization, solve a family of packings in a superellipse container |x-0.5|^p + |y-0.5|^p <= 0.5^p scaled to fit, with exponent p annealed from 2 (disk) to a large value (about 40, near the square). Implement containment as a constraint on each circle center: for the sampled boundary, use the existing wall constraint generalized to the superellipse via the smooth approximation |x-0.5|^p and |y-0.5|^p with p fixed per stage. Warm-start each stage from the previous optimum, and at the final stage restore the exact square walls and run the existing _optimize and _repair. This gives a continuous path through differently shaped containers that may reach a different basin.
backlog.title: Superellipse container homotopy from disk to square

backlog.spec: Solve the packing through its Lagrangian dual: for fixed centers, the radii sub-problem is an LP as before, but instead of enforcing pair constraints directly, maintain a multiplier lambda_ij >= 0 for each near pair (gap below 0.1). Iterate: solve the penalized problem max sum r - sum lambda_ij (r_i + r_j - d_ij) by linprog with the walls kept hard, then update lambda_ij <- max(0, lambda_ij + step * violation) with a diminishing step of 0.5/(k+1), for 60 iterations. Use the final centers from a dual-ascent pass over all centers jointly by alternating with a small gradient step on centers (step 0.01 decaying). Finish with _optimize and _repair. Seeded and deterministic.
backlog.title: Lagrangian dual ascent on pair-overlap multipliers

backlog.spec: Modify the basin-hopping loop so its Metropolis temperature is not fixed at 0.01. Track the number of consecutive iterations without a new global best. When that count reaches 25, multiply the temperature by 4 (reheat, capped at 0.05) and reset the counter, and when a new global best appears, decay the temperature by 0.9 toward a floor of 0.002. Perturbation scale stays at 0.1 for 1 to 3 centers. Run a fixed 200 iterations as before, seeded, and return the global best. This is a schedule that adapts to stagnation rather than being time-driven.
backlog.title: Stagnation-triggered reheating of the basin-hopping temperature

backlog.spec: After any packing is found, compute a Delaunay triangulation of its centers (scipy.spatial.Delaunay) and take the set of edges in the triangulation plus any pair with center distance below 0.35. Rebuild the joint SLSQP in _optimize so that pair non-overlap constraints are only generated for these pairs, with the wall constraints unchanged. After the restricted solve, check all 325 pairs with _repair (which already handles every pair) so the final packing is valid. Use this for a sweep of basin-hopping moves to cut the constraint count and let the solver take more iterations within the time budget.
backlog.title: Delaunay-restricted constraint set for the joint solve

backlog.spec: Build a fresh starting configuration without any optimizer. Using a fixed seed, draw about 4000 random candidate points in [0,1]^2. Place circles one at a time in decreasing target-radius order (for example 0.16 down to 0.08 with random jitter). Each circle goes at the candidate that maximises its feasible radius, where feasible radius = min(wall distance, distance to placed circles minus their radii). Keep the best of several seeds by final greedy sum. Pass the result to the existing joint SLSQP and repair path as one more start family, with its own seed range.
backlog.title: Greedy largest-first hole placement start

backlog.spec: Generate starts by recursive corner filling. Place the largest circle in one random corner of the square, tangent to both walls. Then repeatedly place the next largest circle tangent to two existing objects (two walls, or one wall and one circle, or two circles) at a randomly chosen free corner-gap, until 26 circles are placed or no gap fits a radius above 0.03. Randomise the choice of corner and the size sequence with a fixed seed. Hand the centers and radii to the existing joint SLSQP and repair. This adds a cascade family alongside the random and symmetric starts.
backlog.title: Recursive corner-cascade (Apollonian-style) start

backlog.spec: Enumerate integer partitions of 26 into 4 to 6 horizontal rows, with each row count between 3 and 7. For each partition, place circles in evenly spaced rows, with alternate rows offset by half a spacing and small seeded jitter. Assign radii from the row spacing, with a larger value for the middle rows. Run the joint SLSQP and repair on each partition, plus transposed (vertical) versions. Keep the best feasible result. The enumeration is deterministic and finite, so it adds a fixed batch of starts with no timing dependence.
backlog.title: Row-partition enumeration starts

backlog.spec: Treat the radius class of each circle as a discrete variable. Assign every circle one of three classes (large, medium, small) with a fixed seeded random draw, then run joint SLSQP starting from class-based initial radii 0.13, 0.09 and 0.06. Run simulated annealing on the class labels: swap the labels of two circles, or relabel one circle, then re-solve. Accept or reject with a Metropolis rule on the resulting sum. Keep the best packing across all evaluated labelings. Do not fix the radii inside the solve; only the initial labels are discrete.
backlog.title: Discrete radius-class assignment search

backlog.spec: Add a new move to the basin-hopping loop. Pick a random centre point and select the 3 to 6 circles nearest to it. Rotate their centres about that point by a random angle drawn from [-0.6, 0.6] radians, and keep them inside the square by clipping. Leave the other circles fixed for the initial projection. Then re-solve with joint SLSQP and repair. Keep the existing single-circle perturbation as the other move, and choose between the two moves with a seeded coin flip. This moves whole local neighbourhoods, which single-centre jitter cannot do.
backlog.title: Rotating-cluster basin-hopping move

backlog.spec: Maintain a tabu list of visited packings during basin hopping. Each packing gets a signature: its sorted radii rounded to 2 decimals, plus the number of contacts rounded. Before accepting a new candidate, check whether its signature is in the tabu set; if so, reject it and draw a new perturbation. Add each accepted state's signature to the set. The list has a fixed capacity of 200, with first-in-first-out eviction. The rest of the basin-hopping loop, including the Metropolis step, stays unchanged. This forces exploration of new basins instead of cycling among near-duplicates.
backlog.title: Tabu memory over packing signatures

backlog.spec: Add a topology-changing move to basin hopping. Merge: remove the two smallest circles and insert one circle at their weighted-average position, with radius equal to the sum of their areas' equivalent radius. Re-solve the 25-circle problem with joint SLSQP and repair. Split: take the largest circle and replace it with two circles of radius scaled by 1/sqrt(2), placed at offsets of plus and minus one radius along a random direction. Re-solve the 26-circle joint SLSQP and repair. Accept the candidate with the Metropolis rule used by the basin-hopping loop. Each move is chosen with a seeded random draw.
backlog.title: Split-and-merge topology move

backlog.spec: Add a global perturbation to basin hopping. From the current best packing, contract all centres toward (0.5, 0.5) by a random factor in [0.85, 0.95], and set each radius to 0.9 of its current value. Then re-solve with joint SLSQP and repair. Alternate between contraction and expansion (scale the centres away from the centre by a factor in [1.02, 1.08], clipped to the square) on successive hops. Use the same Metropolis acceptance and seeded random draws. This perturbs the global density of the packing, which the local single-circle moves do not reach.
backlog.title: Contraction-expansion global perturbation

backlog.spec: Make the basin-hopping perturbation scale adaptive. Start with a Gaussian step standard deviation of 0.1 for centre moves. Track the acceptance rate over a sliding window of 20 hops. If the acceptance rate exceeds 0.4, multiply the step by 1.2; if it is below 0.15, multiply it by 0.8. Clip the step to the range [0.01, 0.3]. Keep the number of moved circles seeded and random, and keep the joint SLSQP re-solve and repair unchanged. This lets the search widen when it is stuck and narrow when it is near a good basin, without a fixed schedule.
backlog.title: Adaptive basin-hopping step size

backlog.spec: Add a restart family in which circles sink under a gravity-like bias before a free solve. Give every circle a downward drift of 0.02 per relaxation step toward y=0, with a horizontal shear term that depends on the seeded random offset of each circle. Clip to the square after every step. Run 30 such steps, then release the bias and run joint SLSQP and repair from the resulting centres. Use a different seeded random bias direction for each start. This tests whether a biased compaction reaches basins that isotropic starts miss, with no change to the solver stages.
backlog.title: Gravity-sag restart with release

backlog.spec: In the random multi-start loop, replace the bimodal radius seeds with a power-law profile: draw alpha uniformly from [0.3, 1.2] per start, set r0 sorted descending as r_i = (i+1)^(-alpha), rescale so the initial sum is about 2.5 divided by 26 times the expected count, multiply by U[0.95, 1.05] noise, then run the existing _relax and _optimize calls unchanged. Keep the seeded rng and the 12-start count so the run stays deterministic.
backlog.title: Power-law seeded radii for multi-start

backlog.spec: Add a second local solver that does not use SLSQP. Starting from the current centers and radii, repeatedly linearize all pair constraints (r_i + r_j <= dist_ij) and wall constraints at the current point, solve the LP with scipy linprog (HiGHS) maximizing sum r over a box trust region of half-width delta on x, y, and r, accept the step if the true max-feasible radii sum improves (use _repair to score), otherwise shrink delta by 0.5; grow delta by 1.5 on success. Run it for about 60 iterations from the best SLSQP packing and keep the better of the two results.
backlog.title: Trust-region sequential LP solver over (x, y, r)

backlog.spec: Inside _optimize, reparametrize the decision vector so every variable is O(1) and every constraint row is O(1): use z = (x - 0.5) / 0.5 for centers, and divide the pair constraints by a characteristic length 0.2 (so the pair residual is dist^2 - (r_i+r_j)^2 scaled by 1/0.04) and the wall constraints by 0.1. Pass the analytic Jacobian through the same chain rule. Then run a second SLSQP pass from the rescaled solution with ftol 1e-14 and maxiter 500 to tighten convergence, and map back before _repair.
backlog.title: Rescaled variables and normalized constraints for SLSQP

backlog.spec: The current SLSQP caps every radius at 0.5. Instead run three stages of _optimize with the upper bound on radii set to 0.14, then 0.20, then 0.5, warm-starting each stage from the previous centers and radii (clipped to the new cap). This forces the solver to first settle a dense arrangement of medium circles before letting a few large ones grow, which changes which basin the joint solve lands in. Apply this schedule to the random multi-start starts only; leave the mirror-symmetric phase unchanged.
backlog.title: Staged radius-cap annealing schedule

backlog.spec: Add a new perturbation type to the basin-hopping loop alongside the Gaussian kick. With probability 0.3, pick one circle whose radius is within 1e-3 of its wall-limited maximum (touching a wall), move its center along that wall to a uniformly random position in [r, 1-r] on the same wall, keeping the other coordinate fixed, then run the usual _optimize and _repair. Keep the existing Metropolis acceptance and the seeded rng.
backlog.title: Wall-slide move in basin hopping

backlog.spec: Before the multi-start SLSQP, relax random initial centers under a pairwise Coulomb-like energy E = sum over pairs of 1/d^p plus a wall image term of the same form, with exponent p annealed from 1 to 6 over 200 gradient steps (step size 0.002, clipped to [0,1]). Use the analytic gradient in numpy with vectorized pair arrays, not the loop code. Feed the resulting centers to _optimize with radii seeded at 0.5 times the nearest-neighbour distance. This is a different spreading physics from the existing radius-scaled repulsion and gives the SLSQP a well-spread start.
backlog.title: Coulomb pre-spreading with annealed exponent

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, generate 48 candidate perturbations of the current best centers per outer step (each moves 1 to 3 circles with Gaussian noise). Score every candidate in a single vectorized numpy pass that computes all pair distances with broadcasting and the wall-limited radii, using a greedy feasible-sum proxy (sum of min(wall bound, half the nearest-neighbour gap)). Run the full _optimize only on the top 4 candidates by proxy score. This spends the same wall time on many more kicks and keeps the seeded rng.
backlog.title: Vectorized pre-screen of basin-hopping kicks

backlog.spec: Remove the hard wall inequalities from the solver by parametrizing centers through a smooth bounded map: x = 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(u) and y = 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(v), with u, v free. Keep the radius variables and only the pairwise non-overlap constraints in SLSQP, and enforce containment through the parametrization plus a radius bound r <= min(x, 1-x, y, 1-y) computed as one inequality per circle. Build the Jacobian with the chain-rule factor cos(u)/2. This changes the constraint geometry the solver sees near walls and may let circles slide into corners that the hard-bound formulation handles poorly.
backlog.title: Reflective wall reparametrization for SLSQP

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed split between the symmetric phase, the random multi-start, and basin hopping with a UCB1 bandit over three arms: mirror-symmetric search, random multi-start, and basin hopping from the current best. Each pull of an arm runs one unit of that arm's work (one symmetric search, one random start, or 10 basin-hopping steps from the current best) and records the reward as the improvement in best sum divided by the unit cost. Use the seeded rng for tie-breaking, a total of 30 pulls, and an exploration constant of 0.5. The wall-clock guard remains as a safety cutoff only.
backlog.title: Bandit allocation over start families

backlog.spec: Add a data-driven start family that builds a packing by random sequential adsorption: draw candidate points uniformly in the square, and for each candidate in order accept it as a new circle center with radius equal to the largest value that keeps it inside the square and at least a gap of 0 from accepted circles (min of wall distance and half the distance to the nearest accepted circle, minus any accepted radius constraint); keep going until 26 circles are placed, skipping candidates with radius below 0.03. Then run _optimize on the result and _repair. Use the seeded rng and run this family for about a third of the random starts, with the rest using the current starts.
backlog.title: Random sequential adsorption start

backlog.spec: Replace the SLSQP polish in _optimize with a trust-region sequential linear program. At each iteration, linearize all pair constraints (dx^2+dy^2 >= (ri+rj)^2 becomes a linear cut around the current point) and the containment constraints, then solve max sum(r) over a box step |delta| <= Delta using scipy.optimize.linprog(method='highs'). Accept the step if the true nonlinear max violation drops below 1e-9 and the sum of radii improves; otherwise shrink Delta by 0.5. Grow Delta by 1.5 after accepted steps. Stop when Delta < 1e-7 or after 60 iterations. Keep the existing _repair call afterwards so the output is always feasible. Use it as the polish for the best 3 SLSQP results from the multi-start.
backlog.title: Trust-region sequential LP over (x, y, r)

backlog.spec: In _optimize and the symmetric solver, change the variables to be O(1) and well conditioned. Use z = (x, y, r) divided by a fixed scale of 1 for positions and 0.1 for radii, so the solver sees radii near 1. Write each pair constraint as 1 - (dx^2+dy^2)/(ri+rj)^2 >= 0 scaled by the mean squared radius, and each containment constraint as (x - r)/0.1 >= 0 style. Provide the matching analytic Jacobians and keep ftol 1e-12 with maxiter 500. Run it on the same 12 random starts as before and keep the best result. The goal is that SLSQP converges to a tighter local optimum on the same starts, which the current unscaled problem may miss.
backlog.title: Rescaled variables and normalized constraints for SLSQP

backlog.spec: Before any continuous solve, fix a radius-class template: for example 2 large circles, 6 medium and 18 small, with class sizes drawn from a seeded list of 3 to 4 templates. Generate an initial assignment that places classes at random centers, then run a short swap search over class labels (exchange the classes of two circles, accept if the SLSQP result improves on a cheap LP-radius score). Run the joint SLSQP only on the best 2 assignments. Initialize radii from the assigned class values scaled to be feasible. This explores the large-versus-small topology directly rather than through random bimodal seeds.
backlog.title: Discrete radius-class assignment search

backlog.spec: Within _optimize, build the pair-constraint index set from the Delaunay triangulation of the starting centers (scipy.spatial.Delaunay, take each triangle edge plus pairs closer than 0.35) instead of all 325 pairs. This shrinks the SLSQP Jacobian by about 5x and allows more starts within the time budget. After the solve, check all pairs with _repair; if any pair overlaps by more than 1e-6, add that pair to the set and re-solve once. Use the time saved to increase the random multi-start count from 12 to 24 while keeping the 200 s cap. The goal is more global exploration at the same wall time.
backlog.title: Delaunay-restricted constraint set for fast joint solves

backlog.spec: Add a data-driven start generator based on random sequential adsorption. Seed an RNG and place circles one at a time: sample 300 random candidate points, compute for each the largest radius that fits against the walls and the already placed circles (min of distance to walls and distance to placed centers minus their radius), keep the point with the largest feasible radius, capped at 0.12, and place the circle there. Repeat for all 26 circles. Use the resulting centers and radii as the SLSQP start for a quarter of the multi-start slots. This produces jammed, irregular layouts with a mix of sizes, different from the uniform and ring starts already tried.
backlog.title: Random sequential adsorption start family

backlog.spec: Add a new perturbation to the basin-hopping loop. Pick a random center point and select the 4 to 7 circles nearest to it as a cluster. Rotate the cluster's centers about their centroid by a seeded random angle drawn from U[-0.6, 0.6] radians, keep all centers inside [0, 1] by clipping, and reset their radii to 0.8 times the current values. Then run _optimize and _repair as usual, with the Metropolis acceptance unchanged. Choose the rotation move with probability 0.3 and keep the existing Gaussian kick otherwise. This moves whole local clusters past one another, which single-circle jitter cannot do.
backlog.title: Rotating-cluster basin-hopping move

backlog.spec: Turn the upper bound on radii into a schedule. In _optimize, instead of the fixed bound 0.5, run three SLSQP solves in sequence with a per-circle radius upper bound of 0.09, then 0.15, then 0.5, each warm-started from the previous result and each with the constraints unchanged. The early small cap prevents large circles from locking in a poor topology before the small circles have spread out. Apply this schedule to the multi-start and to the basin-hopping solves (the cap schedule can be shortened to two stages in basin hopping). Keep the final _repair step unchanged.
backlog.title: Staged radius-cap annealing inside SLSQP

backlog.spec: Define a container constraint |x-0.5|^p + |y-0.5|^p <= 0.5^p with p annealed in stages from p = 2 (disk-like) to p = 40 (square) over 4 to 5 stages. At each stage, run a joint SLSQP solve where the containment constraints are replaced by the superellipse constraint on each circle center offset by its radius, using a smooth approximation of the boundary, warm-started from the previous stage. After the final stage (p large), run the standard square-container _optimize solve and _repair. Use this for 4 seeded starts. The idea is that a rounded container lets circles rearrange globally before the corners and edges become binding, which can reach a different basin than starting in the square.
backlog.title: Superellipse container homotopy from disk to square

backlog.spec: Replace part of the random multi-start with a (1+lambda) evolution strategy over the 52 center coordinates. Start from the current best packing. Each generation draws lambda = 12 children by adding Gaussian noise with a per-generation sigma that starts at 0.05 and is multiplied by 0.9 on failure and 1.2 on success (one-fifth success rule). For each child, compute the radii with a single linprog(method='highs') solve that maximizes sum(r) subject to the pair and wall constraints at fixed centers, which is cheap compared with SLSQP. Keep the child if its LP sum beats the parent. Run for a fixed 150 generations with the seed 2024. Finish with one _optimize polish of the best center set and _repair.
backlog.title: Evolution-strategy outer search over centers with inner LP radii

backlog.spec: Add a multi-start family that seeds centers along an Archimedean spiral r(theta)=a+b*theta starting near the center and winding outward, with a, b, and the angular offset drawn from the seeded rng and points rescaled into [0.05, 0.95]^2. Initial radii are set to a seeded decreasing profile (large near the center, small at the rim). Each spiral start goes through the existing _relax then _optimize then _repair path. Replace 3 of the 12 uniform-random starts with spiral starts and keep the best feasible packing as before.
backlog.title: Archimedean spiral start family

backlog.spec: Before the final joint solve, run _optimize in a rectangle [0, a] x [0, 1] with a seeded aspect a drawn from U[0.85, 1.15] (scale the bounds in the bounds list and the 1-x, 1-y terms in the constraints accordingly). Solve for a fixed set of aspect values in sequence, warm-starting each solve from the previous one and rescaling x by 1/a so the configuration is carried to the unit square. Finish with a standard unit-square _optimize and _repair on the rescaled result. This lets the packing reorganize topology under a smooth change of container shape.
backlog.title: Anisotropic container homotopy

backlog.spec: Add a new basin-hopping move type alongside the existing Gaussian kick. Pick a seeded random line through the square (vertical, horizontal, or diagonal through a random offset), select the circles on one side of the line, and reflect those centers across the line. Radii are kept, the configuration is clipped to [0, 1]^2, and the result is passed through _optimize and _repair. Accept or reject with the existing Metropolis rule. Use this move with probability 0.25 and the Gaussian kick otherwise.
backlog.title: Reflection move in basin hopping

backlog.spec: Add a basin-hopping move that picks a seeded horizontal or vertical band of width about 2 times the median radius of the current best packing. Shift all centers inside the band by a seeded offset of up to half the median radius along the band direction, clip to [0, 1]^2, then run _optimize and _repair. This creates a row dislocation that the Gaussian kick cannot produce, and the Metropolis test decides acceptance as before.
backlog.title: Shear dislocation move

backlog.spec: After the random multi-start phase, take the best packing and create candidate starts that keep the center positions but permute the radii among circles. Use seeded random transpositions of 2 to 4 radius labels, favouring swaps between circles at different distances from the square's center. Each candidate starts from the permuted radii and goes through _optimize and _repair. Run a fixed budget of 10 such candidates and keep the best feasible packing. This explores size-to-position assignment without changing the geometry.
backlog.title: Size-permutation restarts

backlog.spec: Replace the pure maximize-sum objective in the final stage with a feasibility homotopy. Pick a target T from the current best sum plus 0.002, then solve SLSQP with the constraint sum(r) minus T greater than or equal to 0 and a zero objective, starting from the best packing. If the solve is feasible after _repair with a sum above the incumbent, accept it and raise T by 0.002. Otherwise lower the step to 0.0005 and retry, for at most 15 solves. This pushes the sum up in small verified increments and avoids the flat region at the top of the objective.
backlog.title: Threshold-continuation feasibility solve

backlog.spec: In the final polish, run _optimize 6 times from the best packing, each time with the containment and pair constraint right-hand sides perturbed by seeded Gaussian noise of scale 1e-4. Pass each noisy solution through _repair to obtain a valid packing and record its sum. Use the best valid packing as the new incumbent, and also try a plain _optimize from the mean of the 6 center sets. This smooths the local landscape and can move the solver to a neighboring, higher-sum contact graph.
backlog.title: Randomized-smoothing SLSQP averaging

backlog.spec: Add a start family in which the radius of each seed is set by a two-tier profile: a seeded number k in {3,4,5} of large circles is placed on a ring of radius 0.3 to 0.35 around the center, and the remaining circles are distributed on an outer region with small radii. Initialize radii to 0.13 for the inner tier and 0.06 for the outer tier with seeded jitter, then run _relax and _optimize. Use this as an additional start family in place of 2 of the uniform-random starts. It diversifies the size hierarchy seen by the solver.
backlog.title: Two-tier radial profile seeds

backlog.spec: Split the 26 circles into four spatial quadrants using the current best packing's centers, with the counts per quadrant seeded from {6, 7}. Optimize each quadrant as a standalone square subproblem with the quadrant's circles confined to its region, using _optimize on the reduced set. Then stitch the four sub-solutions into a full 26-circle start by translating them into the unit square and run the global _optimize and _repair on the stitched configuration. This gives a structurally different start from the global random multi-start.
backlog.title: Quadrant-split decomposition solve

backlog.spec: Add a small bonus term to the SLSQP objective that rewards near-tight pairs: for each pair with gap below 0.02, subtract a penalty weight of 0.001 times the squared gap from the objective, and use the same constraint set. Run this regularized solve from the best packing in the basin-hopping phase only. After it converges, run a plain _optimize without the bonus and _repair on the result, and keep it only if the sum is larger. This encourages rigid contact networks that the unbiased solve may leave loose.
backlog.title: Contact-count bonus regularizer

backlog.spec: Keep the existing basin-hopping loop, but run kick evaluations with a cheap SLSQP (maxiter about 60, ftol about 1e-6) so more kicks fit in the time budget. Only when a cheap candidate's sum comes within about 0.01 of the incumbent, re-solve it with the full settings (maxiter 300, ftol 1e-12) and _repair it before the accept/reject test. Keep the same Metropolis rule and seed, and cap the total wall time so the job finishes within about 4 minutes.
backlog.title: Precision-tiered basin hopping

backlog.spec: Replace the blanket r*(1-1e-9) margin in _repair with an exact final scale. For the best packing, compute the smallest pairwise slack ratio (d_ij / (r_i + r_j)) and the wall slack for each circle, then find the largest global factor s in (0.999999, 1] by bisection such that all constraints hold in double precision when radii are multiplied by s. Use a 1e-12 safety gap on the final check. This recovers the lost radius mass of about 1e-8 per circle while keeping the packing strictly valid.
backlog.title: Exact feasibility scaling instead of fixed shrink

backlog.spec: Each basin-hopping step, choose a random center point and remove the 5 to 7 circles nearest to it (the ruin). Re-insert them one at a time, largest first, at the point maximizing the distance to existing circles and walls (the recreate, found by a coarse grid search over the square). Then run the joint _optimize and _repair on the full packing and apply the usual Metropolis acceptance. Use the same seeded RNG and keep the best packing seen.
backlog.title: Ruin-and-recreate in a random disk

backlog.spec: Take the top 4 distinct feasible packings found so far. For each one, apply the 8 symmetries of the square (the dihedral group) and, for every pairing with the reference packing, match the circles by a Hungarian assignment on center distance. Average the aligned centers and radii over the group to form a new seed, then run _optimize and _repair on that seed. Add the result to the candidate pool and keep it only if it improves the best sum. Use a fixed seed for the alignment and the tie-breaking.
backlog.title: Dihedral-aligned consensus seed

backlog.spec: Start from a random feasible packing with equal small radii. Run hard-disk Monte Carlo: propose random displacements of each center with a step that adapts to keep about a 40 percent acceptance rate, and accept only moves that keep all pairs and walls non-overlapping at the current radii. After each sweep, grow every radius to its current feasible maximum (the minimum of wall slack and half the nearest-neighbour gap) so the packing compresses slowly. Stop after a fixed number of sweeps, then pass the result to _optimize and _repair. Use a fixed seed.
backlog.title: Hard-disk Monte Carlo compression

backlog.spec: Build a starting layout by recursively cutting the unit square with random horizontal or vertical guillotine cuts, splitting the 26 circles between the two sub-rectangles in proportion to their areas. Fill each leaf rectangle with a small hex or square grid sized to its circle count, scaled to fit inside it. Use a fixed seed to draw the cut positions and the split ratios. Feed the resulting centers, with radii set to 0.9 times the local cell half-width, into _optimize and _repair as one more multi-start candidate.
backlog.title: Guillotine recursive partition start

backlog.spec: After a joint SLSQP solve, read the Lagrange multipliers of the pair and wall constraints (or estimate them from the active set with a least-squares fit to the gradient of the sum of radii). Compute, for each circle, the gradient of the sum of radii with respect to its center, which is the sum of the multiplier-weighted constraint gradients. In the next basin-hopping kick, move the 1 to 3 circles with the largest gradient norm along that gradient, with a step of about 0.02 plus a seeded random term, instead of an isotropic Gaussian. Then re-solve and keep the usual Metropolis acceptance.
backlog.title: Multiplier-weighted sensitivity kick

backlog.spec: In _optimize, replace the radius variables r with r = exp(u), so that positivity is built in and the radius bounds are dropped. Chain-rule the Jacobian of the pair and wall constraints with respect to u by multiplying the r-columns by r. Start u from log of the current radii, with a floor of 1e-3 on r. Run SLSQP with the same ftol and maxiter, then recover r = exp(u) and apply _repair. Compare this against the existing parametrization in the multi-start loop and keep whichever yields the larger best sum.
backlog.title: Log-radius reparametrization for SLSQP

backlog.spec: Before the multi-start loop, build a candidate where the circles nearest each of the four walls are pinned to touch that wall, with radius equal to their distance to the wall. Pick the pinned set by a seeded random choice of 4 to 6 circles per wall, with corners shared. Place the remaining circles uniformly at random, then run _relax and _optimize on the full set with the pinned circles' contact-with-wall constraint kept as an equality for the first 50 SLSQP iterations and released afterwards. Keep the result only if it beats the current best.
backlog.title: Edge-pinned contact start

backlog.spec: Run the joint SLSQP with the upper radius bound starting at 0.1 for all circles and raise it in three stages (0.1, 0.2, 0.5). Between stages, re-solve with the new bound using the previous solution as the warm start. This lets many small circles settle into the packing before any large circle claims space, which may favour a different basin than the unconstrained start. Apply _repair after the final stage and keep the packing only if its sum beats the current best.
backlog.title: Size-annealed radius-cap continuation

backlog.spec: After the final _optimize call on the best packing, build a finite-difference Hessian of the penalty-augmented objective (sum of radii minus a weighted sum of squared constraint violations) over the 78 variables (x, y, r) at the returned point. If the Hessian has eigenvalues below -1e-6 in the active subspace, take the 2 most negative eigenvectors, displace the solution by a seeded step of size 0.02 along random positive combinations of them, clip to the box, and re-run _optimize and _repair. Accept only if the sum of radii improves. Repeat at most 5 times. This targets saddle points that SLSQP can stall on.
backlog.title: Saddle escape via Hessian eigenvector kicks

backlog.spec: Starting from the best packing, sweep over circles in random order (seeded). For each circle i, hold all others fixed and evaluate a 60x60 grid of candidate centers over [0,1]^2. For each candidate, compute the largest feasible radius as min(wall distance, distance to each other circle minus that circle's radius), then pick the candidate with the largest radius. Move the circle there if it increases the total radius sum after a repair step. Iterate the sweep until no circle moves, then polish with _optimize and _repair. This is a coordinate-wise best-response method that is not gradient based.
backlog.title: Best-response grid sweep for single circles

backlog.spec: Generate starts by first packing 26 circles on a unit torus, where distances wrap around modulo 1 so there are no wall boundaries. Use a seeded soft-repulsion relaxation with periodic distances and radii fixed at a common value chosen so the packing is dense. Then map the torus positions into the square by scaling them into [r, 1-r] with a shrink factor of 0.9 around the center, and hand the result to _optimize with the usual wall constraints. Run this as one additional start family in the multi-start loop, with a fixed count of 3 starts.
backlog.title: Torus-to-square unfolding start

backlog.spec: Replace the four linear wall constraints inside the SLSQP cost with image-charge constraints. For each circle i, create mirror images across the four walls at positions (-x_i, y_i), (2-x_i, y_i), (x_i, -y_i), (x_i, 2-y_i), each with the same radius r_i. Enforce non-overlap between each circle and the images of all other circles via the existing pair constraint form, so containment becomes a pairwise rule. Solve with SLSQP on (x, y, r) as before, using analytic Jacobians. Use this solver variant for the final 4 polish steps of the best packing and keep the best feasible result after repair.
backlog.title: Image-circle wall reflection penalty

backlog.spec: For each start in one start family (4 of the 12 multi-starts), choose a seeded random rotation angle theta uniform in [0, pi/4] and a lattice spacing s so that about 26 lattice points of a square lattice rotated by theta fall inside [0.1, 0.9]^2. Keep the 26 points closest to the center, jitter each by Gaussian noise of 0.01, and set starting radii to 0.5 times the spacing. Pass these starts through the existing relaxation and joint SLSQP. This covers rotated grid arrangements that the unrotated square-grid and hex starts miss.
backlog.title: Random-angle rotated lattice start

backlog.spec: Before the multi-start loop, draw 60 seeded random start parameter vectors, each giving a scalar descriptor: the number of large seed circles k in {2..10}, the seed radius scale, and the central spread. Run a cheap pipeline (relaxation plus a short SLSQP with maxiter 60) for each. Fit a quadratic response surface from the descriptors to the resulting sum of radii using numpy least squares. Pick the 8 descriptor vectors with the highest predicted sum over a seeded random candidate set of 2000 points, and run the full pipeline on those. Keep the best packing overall.
backlog.title: Surrogate-guided seed selection

backlog.spec: Starting from the best packing, run simultaneous-perturbation stochastic approximation over the 78 variables (x, y, r) for 300 iterations. Each iteration draws a seeded Rademacher vector delta, evaluates the penalized objective (negative sum of radii plus 200 times the squared constraint violations) at z plus c*delta and z minus c*delta, and updates z by a step a_k times the gradient estimate. Use gain sequences a_k = 0.01/(k+1)^0.602 and c_k = 0.01/(k+1)^0.101. Finish with _optimize and _repair on the final iterate and keep it only if the sum of radii is higher.
backlog.title: SPSA refinement of the radius-sum objective

backlog.spec: Build a start family where 8 to 12 circles are pinned to the four walls at seeded positions along each edge, with radii set to their maximum wall-limited values. Place the remaining circles at seeded random interior points. Run the relaxation with the pinned circles' coordinates held fixed (set their step to zero), then release them and run the joint SLSQP. Use this as an alternate start in the multi-start loop for 3 of the 12 starts, so edge contacts are present from the beginning.
backlog.title: Edge-pinned contact start

backlog.spec: In basin hopping, with probability 0.25 pick a seeded random center point and radius uniform in [0.2, 0.35]. Remove all circles whose centers lie inside that disk, and reinsert the same number of circles by placing each one at the point of a seeded 500-point candidate set that maximizes its largest feasible radius given the circles already placed. Then run the joint SLSQP and repair, and apply the usual Metropolis acceptance. This is a larger local perturbation than the existing 1 to 3 center kicks.
backlog.title: Ruin-and-recreate inside a random disk

backlog.spec: Take the best packing and snap all centers to a grid of spacing 1/64, then rerun _optimize from the snapped positions with radii set to the repaired values. Repeat with grid spacings 1/128 and 1/256, each time starting from the previous result. This forces the solver to explore nearby combinatorial contact patterns in a discrete way. Keep the packing with the largest repaired sum of radii across all stages, and fall back to the unsnapped best if no stage improves it.
backlog.title: Quantized coordinate ladder

backlog.spec: Before the joint SLSQP that maximizes sum(r), run a first solve that maximizes a single common radius t, with constraints x_i - t >= 0, 1 - x_i - t >= 0 (same for y), and pair distances >= 2t, using the 26 centers from the start as the initial point. Then warm-start the existing joint SLSQP (maximize sum r) from that equal-radius configuration, with each radius set to t and centers unchanged. Keep the rest of the multi-start and basin-hopping code as is. The point is to reach a different basin than random bimodal radii do. Use the same fixed seed and keep the final shrink-and-repair step.
backlog.title: Max-min radius homotopy before sum-of-radii

backlog.spec: Replace the full set of 325 pair constraints in _optimize with a working set. Start with pairs whose centers are closer than 0.35 plus all wall constraints. Run SLSQP on that working set, then compute all pair slacks at the solution, add any pair with negative slack, and re-solve from the current point. Repeat for at most 4 rounds. Finish with _repair on the full pair set so the result is feasible. This makes each solve cheaper, so the same time budget can cover more basin-hopping kicks. Keep the seeded RNG and the 12-start count.
backlog.title: Lazy pair-constraint generation inside SLSQP

backlog.spec: Add a start family that builds 26 low-discrepancy points on a disk using the golden-angle spiral (theta_k = k*2.39996, rho_k = sqrt((k+0.5)/26)). Map each point from the disk to the square with an area-preserving square-to-disk inverse (Shirley-Chiu style), then scale to [0.08, 0.92]. Use the result as the center start for a joint SLSQP with a seeded radius start of 0.08 plus a small seeded jitter. Use this family for 3 of the 12 random multi-starts and keep the other 9 unchanged.
backlog.title: Area-preserving Fibonacci disk-to-square start

backlog.spec: Enumerate a small set of wall-contact patterns: for each pattern, choose how many circles touch the bottom, top, left and right walls (for example 6-6-6-6 spread along edges with 2 corner circles). For a chosen pattern, add equality constraints that set the wall-touching circles' radii equal to their distance to the relevant wall, and solve the joint SLSQP with those equalities. Seed the centers randomly on the chosen edges. Try about 6 seeded patterns and keep the best feasible packing. This explores topologies the random starts miss because they rarely place circles exactly on the walls.
backlog.title: Wall-contact pattern enumeration with equality constraints

backlog.spec: Add a start family from a random Delaunay triangulation. Draw 22 seeded uniform points in the square, add the four corners and a few edge midpoints, and triangulate with scipy.spatial.Delaunay. For each triangle, take its incenter and inradius, sort by inradius, and use the 26 largest incircle centers as the start. Set the start radii to 0.7 times each inradius, clipped to [0.03, 0.2]. Run relax and joint SLSQP from there. Use this family for 2 of the 12 random multi-starts. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged.
backlog.title: Random Delaunay incircle start

backlog.spec: Change the basin-hopping kick distribution. Each kick draws its displacement from a Cauchy distribution with scale 0.05 per coordinate, clipped to [-0.4, 0.4], instead of Gaussian with sigma 0.1. With probability 0.05, a kick instead moves one randomly chosen circle to a uniform random location in the square. Keep the Metropolis acceptance on the sum and the 200-iteration cap. Heavy tails allow occasional long jumps between basins while most kicks stay local. Use the same seeded RNG.
backlog.title: Cauchy heavy-tailed basin-hopping kicks with rare global relocation

backlog.spec: Before the joint SLSQP, re-express the centers in polar coordinates about (0.5, 0.5): each circle i has an angle phi_i and a radial coordinate rho_i, with x = 0.5 + rho cos(phi) and y = 0.5 + rho sin(phi). Make the SLSQP variables (phi, rho, r) and keep the wall and pair constraints in Cartesian form via the mapping, with Jacobians chained through the map. Start from the Cartesian centers converted to polar. Use the polar solve in the multi-start, and the Cartesian solve for the final basin-hopping polish. The change of coordinates may take different paths through the feasible set near the boundary.
backlog.title: Polar reparametrization of centers for the joint solve

backlog.spec: Add a short annealing pass over the best packing's contact graph. Build the graph of circles whose slack is below 1e-6 after the joint solve. Propose a move that removes one contact by moving one endpoint circle to a random point within 0.15 of a circle it does not touch, then solve for centers and radii with the existing joint SLSQP started from that point. Accept by Metropolis on the sum with temperature 0.005, for at most 40 proposals. Keep the best packing seen. This is different from random-kick basin hopping because each move is chosen by the contact graph rather than by a random displacement.
backlog.title: Contact-graph edge-rewiring annealing with LP radii

backlog.spec: Change the objective of the joint solve from sum(r) to sum(r^p) with p continuing from 0.5 toward 1 over 4 SLSQP calls. At each stage, use the solution of the previous stage as the start. Keep the same wall and pair constraints and the radius cap of 0.5. Stage p=0.5 favours spreading the radii more evenly. The final p=1 call is the true objective, and its result is what the code keeps. Apply this only to the multi-start phase, so the basin-hopping polish stays unchanged.
backlog.title: Power-law radius objective continuation

backlog.spec: Replace the joint SLSQP in one multi-start variant with an alternating scheme. Step A: for fixed centers, solve a linear program that maximizes sum(r) subject to r_i + r_j <= d_ij and r_i <= wall distance. Step B: move each center toward the weighted centroid of its Voronoi cell, with weight equal to its current radius, damped by 0.5. Repeat A and B for 30 rounds and keep the best sum seen. Use scipy linprog with highs for step A. The method is cheap and gives a different path from the SLSQP-based polishes already tried.
backlog.title: Lloyd-LP alternation for radii and centers

backlog.spec: Add a reduced SLSQP search in the spirit of _sym_search, but with the mirror across the diagonal y=x instead of x=0.5. Pick m on-diagonal circles with m in {0, 2, 4, 6} and (26-m)/2 free pairs, where circle i at (x,y) has partner at (y,x) with the same radius. Parametrize the free variables, use the affine expansion A @ v + b as in _sym_layout, solve with SLSQP using the same pair and wall constraints, then run the full joint _optimize and _repair. Use 4 to 6 seeded starts of this family inside the existing symmetric phase, keep the best feasible result, and leave everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Diagonal mirror symmetry search (x,y)->(y,x)

backlog.spec: Add a global outer search using scipy.optimize.dual_annealing over the 52 center coordinates in [0,1]^52, seeded with a fixed seed. The fitness of a center set is minus the sum of radii from a linprog (HiGHS) LP that maximizes sum r subject to r_i + r_j <= d_ij for all pairs and r_i <= wall distance. Cap the call with maxiter or a wall-clock check so it finishes in about 90 seconds. Take the best centers, run the joint _optimize SLSQP polish and _repair, and keep the result only if it beats the incumbent. This is a different global mechanism from DE, CMA and ES because it uses simulated annealing with a local search step.
backlog.title: Dual annealing over centers with LP radii as fitness

backlog.spec: Add a seeded start family in which 3 or 4 anchor circles get random positions and radii of 0.15 to 0.2 and are pinned by setting their x and y bounds to equal values in the SLSQP bounds list, while the remaining circles are free. Solve with _optimize using pinned bounds, then release all pins and re-solve with the full joint _optimize, followed by _repair. Use this family for about a third of the random multi-starts and keep the best feasible packing across all families.
backlog.title: Pinned-anchor starts with staged release

backlog.spec: Keep the best mirror-symmetric (x=0.5) packing from _sym_search as the basin-hopping seed. During basin hopping, each kick is applied to the free half of the circles and mirrored to the other half, so the candidate stays in the symmetric subspace, and it is solved with the reduced symmetric SLSQP via _sym_layout. After a fixed number of accepted steps, release the symmetry and run one full joint _optimize plus _repair on the best symmetric result. Keep the best overall packing by sum of radii.
backlog.title: Symmetric-subspace basin hopping

backlog.spec: Replace the Metropolis acceptance rule in the basin-hopping loop with late-acceptance hill climbing. Keep a circular history buffer of length 50 holding the sum of radii of recent accepted states, initialized from the starting packing. A candidate with sum s is accepted if s >= history[iter mod 50] or s > current sum. After each step, write the current sum into the history slot. Keep the existing kick, joint _optimize, _repair and best-tracking code, with a fixed seed and the same iteration count.
backlog.title: Late-acceptance hill climbing in basin hopping

backlog.spec: Add a seeded start family that solves a 24-circle packing with a multi-start _relax plus _optimize. It then finds the two largest empty regions by sampling about 4000 seeded points and taking the point that maximizes the distance to the nearest center and wall. Place the two extra circles at the two best well-separated points, with initial radius 0.03, and run the full joint _optimize plus _repair on all 26 circles. Apply this family to 2 or 3 of the random multi-starts and keep the best feasible result.
backlog.title: Add-two into the largest holes of a 24-circle optimum

backlog.spec: After the best packing is found, polish it by rescaling the decision variables so that centers are O(1) and radii are O(1) by multiplying radii by 10. Run _optimize with ftol 1e-15 and maxiter 1000 on the rescaled variables, then unscale and call _repair. Repeat the solve from its own output until the sum of radii improves by less than 1e-12 or 5 rounds pass. Keep the new packing only if the repaired sum is larger than the incumbent. Keep the repair shrink margin unchanged so the packing stays valid.
backlog.title: Tight rescaled polish with repeated re-solves

backlog.spec: Keep the top 3 distinct packings from the multi-start and basin-hopping phases. Pick one as reference and match the circles of each other packing to it using scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment on the Euclidean distance matrix between centers. Form consensus centers as the average of matched positions and consensus radii as the average of matched radii. Run _relax on the consensus start, then the joint _optimize and _repair. Keep the result only if it beats the incumbent. This is a different recombination rule from the earlier crossover, because the matching is an optimal assignment, not a random splice.
backlog.title: Hungarian-matched consensus of top packings

backlog.spec: Add a seeded start family in which the initial centers are a linear blend (1 - t) * P_hex + t * P_rand, where P_hex is a 26-point hexagonal-lattice selection inside the square with spacing set so the lattice points cover the square, P_rand are uniform random points, and t is drawn from U[0.2, 0.8] per start. Use the blended points as input to _relax, then the joint _optimize and _repair. Use this family for about a quarter of the random multi-starts and keep the best feasible packing across all families.
backlog.title: Lattice-to-random interpolation start
