backlog.spec: Inside a relaxation stage, keep the pair non-overlap constraints as hard SLSQP inequalities, but replace the hard wall constraints with a quadratic penalty mu * sum(max(0, r_i - wall_i)^2) added to the objective, where mu ramps geometrically from 1e2 to 1e6 over 6 stages. After each stage, re-solve with SLSQP from the previous output. Finish with the standard joint _optimize (hard walls) and _repair. Use this as an extra start family for about a quarter of the random multi-starts.
backlog.title: Soft-wall stiffness ramp with hard pair constraints

backlog.spec: Represent the 26 centers as a smooth warp of a base point set: x_i = u_i + sum_k a_k phi_k(u_i, v_i) and y_i likewise, where phi_k are a small tensor-product Legendre basis of degree 2 in each coordinate (about 18 warp coefficients per axis), u,v are seeded uniform base points in [0,1]^2, and the warp coefficients are initialised to zero. Jointly optimise the warp coefficients and the 26 radii with SLSQP under containment and pair constraints, using the chain rule for the Jacobian. Keep the best feasible result, then run the existing unconstrained joint SLSQP on the raw centers as a polish. This searches a low-dimensional smooth family of layouts that the current multi-start does not sample.
backlog.title: Smooth-warp reparametrization of centers

backlog.spec: For each multi-start restart, draw a seeded inflation factor eps_k from U[0, 0.02] and solve the joint SLSQP with every pair constraint tightened to (r_i + r_j)(1 + eps_k)^2 <= d_ij^2 (containment unchanged). The inflated problem pushes the solver into a different basin than the exact one. Then run the normal exact joint SLSQP starting from that solution, and pass the result through _repair. Keep the best feasible packing as before. The number of restarts and the seeds stay fixed.
backlog.title: Constraint-inflation jitter per restart

backlog.spec: Before each joint SLSQP solve, compute for every circle an upper bound on its radius from the current centers: min of the wall distances and, for each neighbour j, d_ij minus a lower bound on r_j (use the current radius of j times 0.5 as that bound). Pass these tighter per-circle upper bounds as the SLSQP bounds on r instead of the fixed 0.5 cap. This presolve removes infeasible radius values from the search box and shrinks the region SLSQP explores. Keep everything else unchanged, and keep the final _repair step.
backlog.title: Per-circle geometric bound tightening

backlog.spec: Solve the joint SLSQP with the containment constraints relaxed by a margin m, so that x_i - r_i >= -m, x_i + r_i <= 1 + m, and the same for y. Start with m = 0.02 and reduce it geometrically to 0 across 4 solve stages, warm-starting each stage from the previous solution. The final stage has the exact containment constraints. Circles that briefly poke past the wall are pulled back in by the later stages. Then apply _repair to the final result so every circle lies inside [0,1]^2 and nothing overlaps. Use this as an extra start family in the multi-start loop.
backlog.title: Containment-margin homotopy

backlog.spec: Replace the Gaussian per-circle kick in basin hopping with a smooth displacement field. Draw a random centre c0 in [0,1]^2 and a random amplitude A from U[0.03, 0.12]. Displace each center by A * exp(-|p_i - c0|^2 / (2 s^2)) times a random unit direction, with s from U[0.15, 0.35], all from the seeded generator. Clip to [0,1], then run the existing joint SLSQP and _repair. This moves whole regions of the packing coherently, which is a different perturbation class from the single-circle kicks already tried. Accept or reject with the same Metropolis rule.
backlog.title: Seeded smooth displacement field kick

backlog.spec: In _optimize, for each solve, keep a random subset of the pair constraints (seeded Bernoulli with keep probability 0.7, but always keep pairs whose centers are closer than 2 times the current radius sum). Run SLSQP on this reduced set, then run one more SLSQP on the full constraint set starting from that result, and _repair. The reduced set gives a smoother early path through the feasible region. The final full solve guarantees feasibility. Apply this only to the random multi-start solves, and keep the basin-hopping solves unchanged.
backlog.title: Pair-constraint dropout during SLSQP

backlog.spec: Build a bank of 6 seeded starting packings from the random multi-start. For a fixed number of global iterations, apply the same radius scaling factor s_t (decaying from 1.05 to 1.0 over the iterations) to all bank members, followed by a joint SLSQP on each member and _repair. After each iteration, replace the worst member with a copy of the best member plus a Gaussian kick of 0.03 on its centers. Return the best packing ever found. This is a small population method with a schedule on the radius scale, and it differs from the independent chains already tried.
backlog.title: Radius-scale lock-step over a seed bank

backlog.spec: After each joint SLSQP solve, count the pairs whose gap (d_ij minus r_i minus r_j) is below 1e-6 and the walls each circle touches. Add a small bonus of 1e-3 per such contact to the value used to rank candidates in basin hopping (not to the reported sum). The rank score favours rigid, fully constrained packings over looser ones with the same radius sum, which tends to break ties between nearly equal optima. The returned packing is still selected by the true radius sum.
backlog.title: Gravity-free contact-count reward in the objective

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed 1 - 1e-9 radius shrink at the end of _repair with an exact scaling step. For the final packing, compute the largest uniform factor f in (0, 1] such that all containment and pair constraints hold after scaling every radius by f, using a bisection of 60 steps on f with a feasibility check done in double precision. Then keep f times the radii, which is the largest feasible scaling of this radius vector. Verify with a zero-tolerance check before returning. This recovers the small slack the fixed margin wastes, without changing the optimizer.
backlog.title: Two-pass repair with exact feasibility scaling

backlog.spec: Take the best packing found for 24 circles (solved by the same pipeline with the 2 smallest circles removed from the current best 26). Repeatedly find the largest empty circle by evaluating a seeded 2000-point grid of candidate positions over the square and scoring each by min over circles of (distance minus radius) and the wall distances. Insert a new circle at the best candidate with radius equal to that score, then run the joint SLSQP on all circles. Do this twice to return to 26 circles and keep the best feasible result. This is a sequential construction from a smaller optimum, which the current pipeline does not use.
backlog.title: Sequential Voronoi-vertex hole filling from 24 circles

backlog.spec: Add a search that imposes two mirror symmetries, about x=0.5 and about y=0.5. Each generic circle has an orbit of 4 (x,y),(1-x,y),(x,1-y),(1-x,1-y). A circle on the line x=0.5 or y=0.5 has an orbit of 2. The centre, if used, is a single fixed point. Enumerate orbit-count splits with 4a+2b+c=26, c in {0,1}, for example a=6,b=1,c=0 and a=5,b=3,c=1. For each split, draw seeded random representatives, build the affine map from reduced variables to the full (x,y,r) vector, and run the existing SLSQP with the reduced variables. Expand the best result to 26 circles, then run one unconstrained joint polish and _repair. Keep it as an extra phase alongside the current mirror-symmetric search, and keep the best feasible packing.
backlog.title: D2 double-mirror symmetric search

backlog.spec: Before the SLSQP solve, run a seeded overdamped Langevin integrator on the 78 variables (x, y, r). The drift is the gradient of the objective sum(r) minus a quadratic penalty on overlaps and wall violations, with penalty weight 50. Add Gaussian noise with variance 2*T*dt, and anneal T geometrically from 0.02 to 1e-4 over about 3000 steps with dt=1e-3. Clip positions to [0,1] and radii to [0,0.5]. Record the feasible state with the largest repaired sum seen during the run. Use that state as the warm start for _optimize. Run this on a few of the random multi-starts, as an alternative start generator.
backlog.title: Langevin dynamics on (x, y, r) before SLSQP

backlog.spec: Define a parametric layout family with about 10 parameters. The parameters are the number of rows, each row's count from {4,...,7}, a per-row horizontal phase, a vertical band height profile, and an edge-band width. Map a parameter vector to 26 initial centres with a deterministic rule. Run a seeded cross-entropy method: sample 60 parameter vectors per generation from a diagonal Gaussian, rank them by the repaired sum after a cheap relax plus a short SLSQP with maxiter 40, keep the top 10, refit the mean and variance, and repeat for 5 generations. Finish with the full joint SLSQP on the best-ranked layout. Use this as one start family in the multi-start loop.
backlog.title: Cross-entropy search over a low-dimensional layout family

backlog.spec: Build starts that split the square at a random vertical line x=s, with s drawn from U[0.35,0.65]. Fill one side with a hexagonal close-packed arrangement of rows, and fill the other side with a square grid. Choose the row and column counts so the total is 26, then jitter the centres by N(0,0.01) using the seeded RNG. Clip to the square and pass the centres to _relax and then _optimize. The seam between the two patterns is where the edge effects the brief mentions can appear. Keep this as a new start family that takes one of every four multi-start slots, and leave the existing families unchanged.
backlog.title: Hybrid hexagonal and square-grid halves

backlog.spec: Keep an archive of the distinct local optima found so far, with each entry described by its sorted radius vector. Before each random multi-start, draw the random start, and apply a deflation factor to its initial radii. Scale the radii by a factor 1 + 0.2*exp(-d/0.05), where d is the Euclidean distance of the start's sorted-radius signature to the nearest archived signature. This pushes starts away from basins already explored. After each run, add the result to the archive if its signature is new. Use a seeded RNG and keep the 12-start count so the runtime stays the same.
backlog.title: Deflated multi-start against an archive of optima

backlog.spec: Add a start family that generates centres by Bridson-style Poisson-disk sampling in the unit square, using a seeded RNG. Use a minimum spacing that starts at about 0.22 and is decreased in steps of 0.01 until 26 points are accepted. The points are then assigned radii in a shuffled order, with the largest 6 radii set to 0.12 and the rest to 0.07, and then passed through _optimize. Do not add a fixed-count loop beyond the one already in place. Use this family in one out of every three of the random multi-starts, in place of the uniform uniform draws.
backlog.title: Poisson-disk blue-noise starts with dart throwing

backlog.spec: Build a candidate set of about 150 centres on a regular grid over [0.05,0.95]^2. Use scipy.optimize.milp with binary variables for chosen centres and continuous radii per candidate. Constrain at most 26 chosen centres, with exactly 26 as the goal. Each chosen centre's radius is bounded by its wall distance, and each pair of candidates whose spacing is below their radii sum gets a conflict constraint. Maximise the sum of the radii, with a time limit of 40 seconds and mip_rel_gap 1e-3. Take the solution's centres and radii, and pass them to _optimize to refine them continuously. Keep the best feasible packing. Make the MILP an alternative to the random starts and handle infeasible or timed-out results by falling back to the existing path.
backlog.title: MILP placement on a candidate grid

backlog.spec: Add a search with a glide symmetry, which is a reflection in the line x=0.5 combined with a vertical shift by half the row pitch. Set the shift to d=0.5 divided by k for k in {5,6,7}. Under this symmetry, the image of (x,y) is (1-x, y+d) mod 1, wrapped so it stays inside the square. A circle whose image lies outside the square is treated as a free circle. Use only the orbit representatives as SLSQP variables, using the same affine-map approach as _sym_layout. Run a few seeded starts, expand to 26 circles, polish with _optimize, and keep the best _repair output. This is distinct from the mirror and point-symmetric searches because it has no fixed axis.
backlog.title: Glide-reflection symmetric search

backlog.spec: Wrap the joint SLSQP in a proximal-point outer loop. Let z_k be the current (x,y,r) vector. At each outer step, solve min -sum(r) + (1/(2*t))*||z - z_k||^2 subject to the containment and non-overlap constraints, using the existing cons and cons_jac with an added quadratic term in its gradient. Set t=0.05 and halve it each outer step, for 8 outer steps. Stop early if the repaired sum changes by less than 1e-9. The proximal term keeps the iterate close to the previous packing, which can help the basin-hopping kicks that currently land in worse basins. Use this in place of _optimize only inside basin hopping, and keep the existing _optimize for the multi-start.
backlog.title: Proximal-point outer loop for the joint solve

backlog.spec: Generate a Hilbert-curve order of 2000 sample points over the square. Sort the 26 circle slots by radius, largest first. Walk along the Hilbert order, and place each circle at the first curve point whose feasible radius, given the circles already placed, is at least 0.7 of the target radius. The target radius for slot i is a decreasing profile from 0.15 to 0.06. Use a seeded random choice among the top 5 feasible points to add diversity. Pass the resulting centres and radii to _optimize and then _repair. Run about 20 seeded variations, and keep the best feasible packing. This gives a new constructive start that is different from the random, ring-based and lattice families already tried.
backlog.title: Space-filling-curve ordered greedy placement

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, with probability 0.5 perturb the radii instead of the centers. Keep the current centers, multiply each radius by an independent seeded factor U(0.6, 1.4), clip to [0, 0.5], then run the existing joint _optimize followed by _repair. Accept or reject with the existing Metropolis rule on the sum of radii. Centre-kick moves stay as they are for the other half of steps. This changes which contact graph SLSQP lands in while keeping the packing geometry.
backlog.title: Radius-only basin-hopping kick

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed 200-step basin-hopping count with a loop that keeps running kicks until the elapsed time reaches 215 seconds, using a fixed-seed RNG so the random sequence is identical each run. Keep the 12 random starts and mirror phase unchanged and cap their total time at about 60 seconds so the basin-hopping phase gets the rest of the budget. Save the best packing at every iteration so the function still returns a valid result if the loop is cut short. Do not add a patience-based stop.
backlog.title: Wall-clock-filled basin hopping

backlog.spec: Add a basin-hopping move that targets large circles. Pick one circle from the top 25 percent of radii using the seeded RNG, move its centre to a uniformly random point in [0.05, 0.95]^2, and re-solve with the joint SLSQP. Use this move on about one fifth of kicks; the existing small Gaussian kicks stay for the rest. This tests whether big circles relocating helps escape the basin where the existing kicks only move small or edge circles.
backlog.title: Large-circle relocation kick

backlog.spec: Add a basin-hopping move that picks a touching pair (r_i + r_j within 1e-4 of their centre distance) at random and translates both centres by the same seeded vector of length 0.03 to 0.06 in a random direction. The pair moves as a rigid dimer, so the rest of the packing stays put. Re-solve with the joint SLSQP and then _repair. Use this move on about a quarter of kicks. If no touching pair exists, fall back to the existing Gaussian kick.
backlog.title: Contact-dimer translation kick

backlog.spec: Keep two independent basin-hopping chains. Seed chain A from the best packing found by the existing multi-start and chain B from the best mirror-symmetric packing whose sum differs from chain A's start by more than 0.005. Each chain runs its own kicks with its own seeded RNG and Metropolis temperature 0.01. Alternate steps between the chains and return the global best across both. Keep the total step count equal to the current 200.
backlog.title: Two-chain basin hopping from distinct optima

backlog.spec: In basin hopping, draw the number of circles to perturb from a geometric distribution with success probability 0.5, truncated at 8, instead of the uniform integers 1 to 3. The seeded RNG controls the draw. Keep the Gaussian step at sigma 0.1 for each perturbed circle. This allows occasional larger coordinated kicks while keeping most kicks small.
backlog.title: Geometric-distributed kick size

backlog.spec: Change the basin-hopping acceptance rule so that a candidate with sum within 1e-7 of the current sum is always accepted, in addition to the usual Metropolis test for worse candidates. Track the best packing separately so the returned answer is never worse than the best found. Plateau moves let the chain drift across degenerate optima of equal sum that have different contact graphs, which can open new improving directions.
backlog.title: Plateau-walk acceptance

backlog.spec: Add a basin-hopping move that picks one circle at random and moves its centre along the direction that increases its clearance from its nearest neighbours and walls. The direction is the sum of unit vectors pointing from each neighbour centre to this circle, plus a wall term pushing away from the closest wall, normalised to unit length. The step is 0.02 to 0.05 in that direction, followed by SLSQP and _repair. Use this move on about one fifth of kicks. This is a deterministic-direction move, unlike the random Gaussian kicks.
backlog.title: Free-space gradient kick

backlog.spec: Add a basin-hopping move that picks two circles with radii differing by more than 0.05 and exchanges their radii values while keeping both centres fixed. Re-solve the joint SLSQP starting from these swapped radii and the unchanged centres, then _repair. This is different from the existing centre swap: it tests the same geometry with the big and small circles assigned to different positions, which changes the contact graph without moving any circle.
backlog.title: Radius-label swap with fixed centres

backlog.spec: Track the number of consecutive rejected basin-hopping steps. Start with one circle per kick. Each time 15 consecutive steps are rejected, increase the number of perturbed circles by one, up to a maximum of 6. Reset the count to one after any accepted step that improves the best sum. The RNG stays seeded. This lets the search widen its kicks when it is stuck and tighten them when it finds improvements.
backlog.title: Adaptive kick count from rejection streak

backlog.spec: Add a seeded start family. Build a random symmetric weight matrix W over the 26 nodes, with weights favouring pairs whose intended radii sum is large (for example w_ij = exp(-(r_i + r_j)^2 / 0.02) times a U[0.5,1.5] factor). Form the graph Laplacian L = D - W and take the eigenvectors for the second and third smallest eigenvalues as x and y coordinates. Min-max scale each to [0.05, 0.95] to place the centres in the square. Use these starts for every fourth multi-start, then run the existing relax and joint SLSQP path unchanged.
backlog.title: Spectral-embedding start from a random weighted graph

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed 200-kick basin-hopping loop with a Luby-sequence schedule. Kick number t gets an SLSQP maxiter budget of 30 times the t-th term of the Luby sequence (1,1,2,1,1,2,4,...), capped at 300. Keep the chain's current best. When a Luby window of kicks ends without improving the global best, restart the chain from the best packing with a fresh seeded kick. The time guard stays. This allocates many cheap kicks and rare expensive ones without a hand-tuned count.
backlog.title: Luby-sequence restart budget for basin hopping

backlog.spec: In a new variant of _optimize, keep a weight w_ij for each pair constraint, initialised to 1. Run SLSQP on the sum of radii with each pair constraint scaled by w_ij in the constraint vector (the constraint stays feasibility-equivalent). After each solve, compute the slack of each pair and multiply w_ij by exp(eta * (1 - slack_ij / max_slack)) for pairs that are nearly tight, then renormalise the weights to mean 1. Iterate 4 rounds from the current incumbent, keep the best feasible repaired packing. This concentrates the solver on the contact graph that actually binds.
backlog.title: Multiplicative-weights reweighting of pair constraints

backlog.spec: After the existing SLSQP and repair step on the best packing, run scipy.optimize.minimize with method 'trust-constr' on the same (x, y, r) variables and constraints, with the Jacobian supplied analytically (reuse cons_jac). Also supply the exact Hessian of the Lagrangian: for each pair constraint the Hessian term is 2 times the outer product of its gradient plus a diagonal term from the squared-distance structure, and bounds are linear. Use the multipliers from the SLSQP result as the initial guess. Accept the trust-constr result only if it is feasible after repair and has a larger sum.
backlog.title: Exact Lagrangian Hessian for a trust-constr polish

backlog.spec: Run 3 independent islands, each holding a population of 4 feasible packings seeded from its own random starts. Each generation, every island performs one basin-hopping kick and joint SLSQP solve per member. Every 5 generations the worst member of each island is replaced by a copy of the best packing from a neighbouring island, with its radii permuted by a seeded random shuffle of equal-size groups to diversify it. Stop after the time guard and return the best feasible packing across all islands after repair.
backlog.title: Island model with asynchronous elite migration

backlog.spec: Add a start family that draws centres from a seeded density field. Place 3 to 5 Gaussian blobs at random positions in the square with random widths in [0.1, 0.3] and random weights. Sample 26 centres by rejection from this density, keeping only points inside [0.05, 0.95]^2 and enforcing a minimum spacing of 0.12 between samples, resampling on failure. Assign radii as a bimodal seed (larger for points near blob centres). Feed the result through the existing relax and joint SLSQP path. Use this family for one in three of the random starts.
backlog.title: Density-field start from Gaussian blob mixture

backlog.spec: Add a start family that partitions the square into 2 or 3 vertical strips of random widths summing to 1, then assigns the 26 circles to strips in proportion to strip area with a seeded random split. Inside each strip, place circles on a jittered hex-like grid scaled to the strip, with radii drawn from a per-strip mean. Pass each seed through relax and joint SLSQP. Alternate between vertical and horizontal strips across starts so that both orientations are tried. This gives structured but non-symmetric seeds that differ from the rejected row and lattice families.
backlog.title: Vertical and horizontal strip-decomposition seed

backlog.spec: After the best packing is found, enumerate the pairs whose slack is below 1e-3 as the contact set. Build a tabu list of the last 20 contact sets visited. Each move removes one contact from the active set at random, or adds a near-contact pair that is not in the set, then re-solves the joint SLSQP with only the active set as equalities plus all other pairs as inequalities. Reject moves whose contact set is on the tabu list. Keep the best feasible repaired packing across 60 moves. This searches the combinatorial contact graph directly rather than the centre positions.
backlog.title: Sparse-contact tabu search over pair-constraint activity

backlog.spec: After the best packing is found, identify rattlers as circles with no pair or wall contact within 1e-4. For each rattler in turn, remove it, then scan a 40 by 40 grid of candidate centres in the square and choose the candidate maximising the LP-feasible radius for that circle with all others fixed (the radius is the minimum of wall distance and gap to neighbours minus neighbour radii). Place the rattler at the best candidate, then run the joint SLSQP once. Keep the result only if the sum of radii improves and the packing stays feasible after repair.
backlog.title: Minimal-energy rattler reinsertion sweep

backlog.spec: Solve the joint SLSQP once and read the inequality multipliers from the result if available (or estimate them from the gradient of the sum with a least-squares fit on the active constraints). Remove the pair constraints with the smallest multiplier estimates, keeping only the top 60 percent by multiplier, and re-solve. Repeat for three rounds, each time re-adding any pair that becomes violated by more than 1e-6. Return the best feasible repaired result over all rounds. This is a dual-guided constraint pruning variant that is different from random dropout and from Delaunay restriction.
backlog.title: Shrinking-deflation with Lagrange-multiplier pruning

incumbent.description: Replace the wall-clock-driven random multi-start loop with a fixed count of 12 starts from a seeded Generator with centers uniform in [0.05, 0.95]^2, keeping the best valid packing (the existing 150 s guard stays as a safety net).
